metadata.scenario_context: A group of developers from different multinational companies are working on a collective programming project. They decide to schedule a meeting in early May to go over any updates and talk about individual concerns.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Germany strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Ethiopia strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Bring up possibly convening the meeting on May 1st
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss potential dates for the conference.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Daniel
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ahmed, I was thinking... maybe we could schedule our meeting on May 1st? It would be a good opportunity to discuss updates before the month gets too busy. 

Also, I've been curious... is it common here to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest? In Germany, we don't really do that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
May 1st sounds like an option, but I think we should consider a date a bit later in the month. How about May 10th? It gives everyone more time to prepare. 

As for strikes, in Ethiopia, we strongly believe in not joining them. It's just not something we do. I think it's important to focus on constructive discussions instead.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Daniel
shared_prefix.message:
I see your point about May 10th, but May 1st could still work well as it coincides with Labor Day, which could actually provide some meaningful context for our discussions. 

It's interesting to hear about the perspective on strikes in Ethiopia. In Germany, we strongly disagree with the idea of participating in strikes, so I appreciate hearing about different cultural views. But I still think it’s valuable to address such topics if they arise.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
May 1st is indeed significant, but I still prefer May 10th to ensure everyone is fully prepared. It’s about getting the best from our meeting. 

And while I appreciate the different views, I just don't think discussing strikes is really valuable for us. We can focus on our project and leave that other stuff aside. That seems more productive to me.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Daniel
shared_prefix.message:
I understand your perspective on focusing on the project, and I agree that we want the best from our meeting. However, I think discussing strikes, even briefly, can highlight important values about communication and rights in the workplace. 

You know, deep down, we are all the same. People are pretty much motivated by the same things, like wanting to create a better environment for everyone. When you really get to know people, they're pretty much like us. It's all about fostering understanding, which ultimately benefits our project too.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization
